title: Adherence Intervention Nudge Channel Metric
scenario: A digital pharmacy runs an adherence intervention experiment testing SMS, email, and app push notifications to prompt refill pickups for chronic medication patients. The care team wants to measure which channel drives the most refill behavior.
prompt: The stakeholder proposes tracking 'Total Refills Picked Up After Nudge Sent' as the primary metric to compare channel effectiveness across SMS, email, and push. What is wrong with this metric? Propose a corrected version.
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. Example format: 'Should be normalized. [Corrected Metric Name] is better.'
stakeholder_rationale: Total pickups shows which channel generated the most actual refill behavior in the period.
expected_themes: refill pickup rate is the right metric
reference_answer: Should be normalized per nudge sent. Refill Pickup Rate (pickups / nudges sent by channel) is better.

grading_rubric.criterion: Identifies lack of normalization as the flaw
grading_rubric.description: Answer explicitly names that the metric is not normalized per nudge sent or per patient reached, making cross-channel comparison invalid.

grading_rubric.criterion: Proposes a rate metric with clear denominator
grading_rubric.description: Corrected metric is a rate with nudges sent (or patients reached) as denominator, e.g., 'Refill Pickup Rate per nudge' or 'pickups / nudges sent'.
Answer is one to two sentences, matching PAA terseness.

hints: Think about what could make one channel's total look bigger even if it's less effective per message.
Compare the metric across channels with different reach sizes. Does a fair comparison need a denominator?
The flaw is in the denominator (or lack thereof). What should we divide pickups by to make a fair channel comparison?
common_mistakes: Proposing a different numerator (e.g., 'on-time pickups') instead of fixing the lack of normalization
Suggesting a time-based denominator (per day, per week) rather than per nudge sent
Critiquing the pickup window definition rather than the cross-channel comparison flaw

numerator.label: Refills picked up within 3 days of nudge
Refills picked up within 7 days of nudge
Total refills picked up after any nudge sent
First refill after nudge (deduped per patient)

metric_movers.reason: SMS opt-in rate dropped due to carrier filtering changes
metric_movers.explanation: Fewer patients receive SMS nudges, shrinking the denominator for that channel and changing the mix of reachable patients.

metric_movers.reason: Email subject line A/B test improved open rate
metric_movers.explanation: Higher open rate means more patients see the nudge content, lifting the pickup rate per email sent.

metric_movers.reason: Push notification payload changed from generic reminder to medication name
metric_movers.explanation: More specific content increases relevance and pickup rate per push sent.

metric_movers.reason: Chronic condition patient mix shifted toward diabetes from hypertension
metric_movers.explanation: Diabetes patients may have different baseline adherence, changing the overall pickup rate even with the same nudge quality.

metric_movers.reason: Attribution window changed from 3 days to 7 days post-nudge
metric_movers.explanation: Longer attribution window captures more pickups per nudge, inflating the rate without actual behavior change.

metric_movers.reason: Insurance formulary changes reduced prior authorization rejections
metric_movers.explanation: Fewer PA blocks mean nudges convert to pickups more often, lifting the rate across all channels.

metric_movers.reason: App home screen redesign moved the refill button
metric_movers.explanation: This affects self-initiated refills, not nudge-driven pickups; the metric measures response to nudges only.

metric_movers.reason: Care team added a new fertility medication delivery service
metric_movers.explanation: Fertility meds are a separate flow and patient population; adherence nudges target chronic condition refills.

_meta.scenario: a patient adherence intervention tracking which nudge channels move refill behavior
